user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.

messages.content: Hi! How can I help you today?

Hello, I’m having some trouble with my phone. I’ve been trying to send a picture message to my daughter, but it just won’t go through. I’m not very good with these things, so I’m hoping you can help me fix it.

To assist you with the picture messaging issue, I need to identify your account first. Could you please provide me with your phone number or your full name along with your date of birth? This will help me look up your account and check the settings related to your messaging service.
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you also need my date of birth, or is that enough?
For name-based lookup, I do need your date of birth for verification. Since you provided your phone number, I can start by looking up your account using that. Let me check your account details now.

I have found your account, John Smith. To help resolve the issue with sending picture messages (MMS), I will need to check the status of your phone's cellular service, mobile data, and MMS capabilities. 

First, I want to confirm if your phone has cellular service and mobile data enabled. Could you please tell me if you are currently able to make calls and use mobile data on your phone?

I can see that my phone shows full signal bars and it says "5G" at the top, and there’s a little icon that looks like two arrows which I think means data is on. I haven’t tried making a call just now, but the signal looks strong. Is that what you needed to know?

Thank you for the information. It sounds like your phone has good cellular signal and mobile data is likely enabled. To further diagnose the MMS issue, I will check if your phone's messaging app has the necessary permissions to send picture messages and if the MMS settings are correct.

I will start by checking the MMS capability on your phone.
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
It looks like my phone isn’t able to send picture messages right now. Is there something I need to do to fix this? I’m not sure where to look or what to change.

Since your phone is currently unable to send picture messages, I will proceed with a series of checks and fixes to resolve the issue. 

First, I will check your phone's network status to confirm the cellular connection details and mobile data status.

Your line is active, and you have mobile data available with 3.2 GB used out of a 5 GB limit for this billing cycle. Your data connection should support MMS.

Next, I will check your phone's network status and MMS settings to identify any issues preventing picture messages from sending.

Airplane Mode: OFF
SIM Card Status: active
Cellular Connection: connected
Cellular Signal: excellent
Cellular Network Type: 5G
Mobile Data Enabled: Yes
Data Roaming Enabled: No
Wi-Fi Radio: OFF
Wi-Fi Connected: No

Current APN Name: internet
MMSC URL (for picture messages): Not Set
(These are technical settings, usually best left unchanged.)

My phone says it’s connected to the cellular network with excellent signal, and mobile data is on. I also noticed that something called the "MMSC URL" for picture messages isn’t set—does that matter? I’m not sure what that means, but I thought I should mention it.

Yes, the MMSC URL is very important for sending and receiving picture messages (MMS). If it is not set correctly, your phone won't be able to send MMS.

I will guide you to reset your phone's APN settings to restore the correct MMSC URL and other necessary settings. After that, you will need to reboot your phone for the changes to take effect.

Would you like me to proceed with guiding you through resetting the APN settings now?

If you think that will help, then yes, please guide me through it. But I’m a bit nervous—will resetting these settings mess up anything else on my phone? I really don’t want to lose my photos or anything important.

Resetting the APN settings will not delete your photos, contacts, or any personal data on your phone. It only restores the network settings related to your mobile data and messaging service to their default values. This can often fix issues with MMS and mobile data connectivity.

If you're ready, I will guide you through the steps to reset the APN settings and then reboot your phone. This should help fix the picture messaging issue. Would you like to proceed?
Alright, if it won’t delete my photos, I’m willing to try. Please go ahead and tell me what to do, but could you go slowly and explain each step? I get a bit flustered with these things.

I understand, and I will guide you step-by-step carefully.

Step 1: Reset APN Settings
- On your phone, go to the "Settings" app.
- Look for "Network & Internet" or "Connections" and tap on it.
- Find and tap on "Mobile Network" or "Cellular Network."
- Look for "Access Point Names" or "APN."
- There should be an option to "Reset to default" or "Reset APN." Tap on that to reset your APN settings.

Please let me know once you have completed this step, and then I will guide you through rebooting your phone.

APN settings will reset at reboot.
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
I’ve followed your instructions and reset the APN settings. What should I do next? Do I need to restart my phone now? I just want to make sure I’m doing this right.

Yes, now the next step is to restart your phone to apply the new APN settings.

Please power off your phone completely, wait a few seconds, and then turn it back on.

Once your phone has restarted, try sending a picture message again and let me know if it works or if you encounter any issues.

Resetting APN settings...
Restarting network services...
Status Bar: 📶⁴ Excellent | 5G | 📱 Data Enabled | 🔋 80%
Your messaging app cannot send MMS messages.
I restarted my phone like you said, but I still can’t send picture messages. Is there something else we can try? I’m starting to get a bit worried this won’t get fixed.

Let's continue troubleshooting to resolve this.

Next, I want to check if Wi-Fi Calling is enabled on your phone, as sometimes it can interfere with MMS. If it is on, I will guide you to turn it off.

I will also check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send MMS.

Let me start by checking the Wi-Fi Calling status on your phone.
Wi-Fi Calling is currently turned OFF.
It looks like Wi-Fi Calling is already turned off on my phone. What should we check next? I really hope we can get this working soon.

Thank you for confirming that Wi-Fi Calling is off.

Next, I will check if your messaging app has the necessary permissions to send picture messages. This includes permissions for storage and SMS.

I will proceed with checking the app permissions now.

To proceed with checking and adjusting the messaging app permissions on your phone, I need to confirm the exact name of the messaging app you are using. Could you please tell me the name of the app you use to send text and picture messages? For example, is it called "Messages," "Messenger," or something else?
The following apps are installed on the phone: messaging, browser
The app I use is just called “messaging.” That’s the one I always use for my texts and pictures.
